air-bike.description: A full-body conditioning exercise on the air bike, combining pedaling with an arm push-pull for sustained power output.
instructions: Sit on the air bike and grip the moving handles.
Place your feet on the pedals and brace your core.
Push and pull the handles while pedaling at a steady pace.
Drive with both arms and legs to maintain power output.
Continue for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid slumping over the handles.
Breathe rhythmically to sustain effort over longer intervals.
Pull the handles with your back, not just your arms.

assisted-dips.description: A beginner-friendly dip performed on an assisted machine that offsets body weight, training the chest and triceps.
instructions: Step onto the assisted dip machine with knees on the pad.
Grip the parallel bars and support your weight with straight arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until shoulders are below elbows.
Press back up to the start position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring out wide.
Stop the descent if you feel pinching in the shoulders.
Reduce the assistance gradually as pressing strength improves.

balance-dome-crunch.description: A crunch done lying with your lower back on the domed side of a balance dome. The dome lets you start the curl from a slightly extended position, which lengthens the abdominals, and its instability makes the trunk work to keep you steady.
instructions: Place the balance dome on the floor with the domed side up and sit on it, then lie back so your lower back rests on the dome.
Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Put your hands behind your head with your elbows wide, without pulling on your neck.
Curl your shoulders and upper back up toward your hips by shortening the distance between your ribs and your pelvis.
Pause briefly at the top and keep your lower back on the dome.
Lower back slowly to the start and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Lead with the ribcage rather than the head; your hands only support your head.
Do not let the dome roll away; keep your feet planted and your hips still.
Start with a small range and extend further back over the dome as your control improves.

balance-dome-single-leg-stand.description: A balance hold on one leg on a balance dome, with the other knee lifted in front of you. The ankle, calf and hip muscles of the standing leg constantly adjust to the tilting surface, which makes it a demanding balance and rehabilitation exercise.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up, next to a wall or a sturdy support.
Step onto the middle of the dome with one foot and stand tall with your knee slightly bent.
Shift your weight onto that leg and lift the other knee in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Keep your hips level, your chest tall and your eyes on a fixed point ahead.
Hold for the planned time, letting your ankle and calf make small corrections.
Lower the foot, rest and repeat on the other leg.
tips: Learn the two-foot balance dome stand first and keep a wall within reach.
Press the whole foot into the dome and let your toes spread; do not grip the surface with them.
Do not look down at your feet; a fixed point ahead helps your balance.

balance-dome-step-up.description: A single-leg step-up onto a balance dome: you place one foot on the domed top, stand up on it and then step back down. The surface tilts under your foot, so the quadriceps and glutes lift the body while the hips and ankle work to keep you steady.
instructions: Stand facing the balance dome, placed domed side up on a flat floor.
Place one foot flat in the middle of the dome.
Press through the whole foot and straighten that leg to stand up on the dome, bringing your other foot beside it.
Stand tall for a moment and keep your weight centred over the dome.
Step back down with the other foot first, then the working foot.
Complete the planned repetitions on one leg, then switch legs.
tips: Put your foot in the middle of the dome; stepping near the edge makes it tip.
Push through the heel and the whole foot rather than hopping up from the back leg.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand until you can step up and down smoothly.

band-pull-apart.description: A high-volume rear delt and scapular retractor exercise performed by pulling a resistance band apart at shoulder height.
instructions: Stand holding a light resistance band with both hands, arms extended straight in front at shoulder height.
Hands start shoulder-width apart, palms facing down.
Keeping arms straight, pull the band apart by driving the hands out to the sides.
Finish with the band touching your chest and the shoulder blades squeezed together.
Return slowly to the starting position and repeat.
tips: Lead the movement with the little fingers — this externally rotates the shoulders.
Use a band light enough to do 15–30 clean reps; this is a high-rep prehab exercise.

banded-chest-stretch.description: A standing stretch that opens the chest by holding a band behind the back and drawing the arms apart.
instructions: Hold a band behind your back with both hands.
Straighten your arms and draw them apart.
Lift your chest and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

banded-glute-bridge.description: A glute bridge with a loop band placed above the knees. Driving the knees out against the band recruits the gluteus medius alongside the prime glute-max bridge — a cheap accessory that doubles as hip activation.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Place a loop band around both legs just above the knees.
Press the lower back into the floor and brace the core.
Drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift the hips into a bridge — keep the band tension by pushing the knees outward.
At the top, the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Pause briefly.
Lower under control to the start and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The knees want to cave inward — that is the band telling you to push them out.
Stop the lift when your hips are level with your shoulders and knees; do not hyperextend the lower back.
Squeeze hard at the top — a fast, half-rep bridge feels easy because it is.

banded-it-band-stretch.description: A lying stretch that uses a band to draw one leg across the body and target the outer thigh and hip.
instructions: Lie on your back with a band around one raised foot.
Hold the band with the opposite hand.
Draw the straight leg across your body toward the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep both shoulders down on the floor.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the outer thigh.

banded-rear-delt-stretch.description: A standing stretch that targets the rear shoulder by pulling one arm across the body against band tension.
instructions: Loop a band around one arm and hold the other end.
Draw that arm horizontally across your chest.
Use the band to deepen the pull gently.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the working shoulder relaxed and down.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

banded-squat.description: A bodyweight squat with a loop band above the knees to teach knees-out tracking.
instructions: Place a loop band just above the knees.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Push the knees out against the band as you squat down.
Descend until thighs are parallel or below.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Push the knees out against the band the whole rep.
Keep the chest up and the back flat.
Do not let the knees collapse inward.

banded-sumo-walk.description: A wide-stance lateral walk with a loop band around the lower legs, targeting the glute medius and maximus.
instructions: Place a loop band around your lower legs, just above the ankles.
Drop into a quarter squat with feet wider than shoulder-width.
Step sideways in a wide stance, keeping tension on the band.
Bring the trailing foot in only partway so the band stays taut, and keep stepping for the prescribed distance before leading with the other leg.
Stay low throughout — do not stand up between steps.
tips: Keep tension on the band the entire set.
Stay in a quarter-squat — do not stand tall between steps.
Take small, controlled steps with toes pointed slightly out.

barbell-box-squat.description: A back squat with a barbell in which you sit back onto a box or bench at the bottom, pause for a moment and stand up again. The box fixes the depth and teaches you to sit back into the hips, and the brief pause removes the rebound out of the bottom.
instructions: Set a box or bench behind you at a height where your thighs end up about parallel to the floor when you sit on it.
Take the barbell on your upper back, step back and stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width.
Brace your trunk and push your hips back, then lower yourself under control toward the box.
Sit onto the box without dropping onto it, keeping your chest up and your shins close to vertical.
Pause briefly with your muscles still tight, without relaxing your back.
Drive through your whole foot to stand up, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Sit back rather than down; the box should be touched with your hips, not rested on with your weight.
Keep the torso tight in the pause; relaxing on the box is where most back injuries happen.
Use a box that cannot slide, and lower it as you progress until you can squat to full depth.

barbell-front-raise.description: An isolation exercise raising a barbell from the thighs to shoulder height, targeting the front deltoids.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip at thigh level.
Keep your arms straight and core braced.
Raise the barbell in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Use a light weight to avoid swinging the bar up.
Avoid leaning back as the bar rises.
Keep your wrists neutral rather than letting them bend backward.

barbell-overhead-extension.description: This isolation exercise effectively targets the triceps brachii by extending the elbows overhead, promoting muscle hypertrophy and strength.
instructions: Load a barbell with an appropriate weight and stand or sit with a neutral spine.
Grip the barbell with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, and press it overhead.
Slowly lower the barbell behind your head by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stable.
Extend your elbows to press the barbell back to the starting overhead position, squeezing your triceps.
Maintain control throughout the movement, avoiding momentum.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing forward to maximize triceps engagement and protect your shoulders.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to enhance muscle tension and growth.
Avoid arching your lower back excessively; brace your core to maintain stability.

barbell-reverse-lunge.description: A barbell lunge stepping backward instead of forward, keeping the front shin vertical while loading the quads and glutes.
instructions: Place a barbell across your upper back and stand tall.
Step one foot backward into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the ground under control.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Step back far enough to keep your front shin close to vertical.
Lower the back knee straight down rather than leaning forward.
Keep your chest tall and hips square throughout.

barbell-zercher-squat-hold.description: An isometric version of the Zercher squat: you squat down with the barbell in the crooks of your elbows and hold the bottom position. The quadriceps, glutes and the trunk stay under tension at the deepest point, while the arms and upper back keep the bar close to you.
instructions: Set a barbell on a rack at about the height of your lower ribs, place the crooks of your elbows under the bar and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lift the bar off the rack, step back and stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your abs and keep your chest tall, then sit down and back until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Stop at the bottom and hold, with your elbows resting inside your knees and your knees pushed out over your toes.
Keep the bar close to your abdomen and your back straight while you hold for the planned time.
Drive up through your feet to stand and return the bar to the rack.
tips: Wrap a towel or a barbell pad around the bar, since it presses into the elbows and the abdomen.
Use safety pins set just below your bottom position, since a long hold at depth is tiring.
Keep the chest tall; if the bar pulls you forward and your back rounds, the weight is too heavy.

bear-plank-hold.description: A static core hold on hands and knees in which the knees hover just above the floor while the back stays flat. It trains the abdominals and shoulders to stabilise the trunk and is a stepping stone to the full plank.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Tuck the toes under and brace the abdominals so the back is flat.
Press into the hands and lift the knees a couple of inches off the floor.
Hold the position with the hips level and the head in line with the spine.
Breathe steadily, then lower the knees to rest.
tips: Keep the knees close to the floor; lifting them higher turns the hold into a pike.
Spread the fingers and push the floor away so the shoulders do not collapse.
Keep the neck long and look at the floor slightly ahead of the hands.

behind-the-neck-pull-ups.description: A wide-grip pull-up pulled high enough that the bar passes behind the head at the top instead of under the chin, which forces the shoulders into end-range external rotation.
instructions: Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and hang at full arm extension with your legs together.
Keep your torso vertical rather than leaning back, and pull your elbows down and out to the sides.
Continue pulling until the bar passes behind your head and the back of your neck comes level with it, without letting the bar touch your neck.
Lower yourself under control back to a full dead hang, keeping your head still rather than letting it snap forward.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: This variation is widely discouraged. Finishing behind the head loads the shoulder at the end of its external rotation, where the joint has the least capacity to protect itself, and any contact between the bar and the neck puts that load through the cervical spine.

A standard or wide-grip pull-up trains the same muscles through the same shoulder range — nothing about back development requires the bar to travel behind the head, so there is no benefit here to trade the risk against.

If you perform it anyway, stop well short of touching the bar to your neck and leave it out entirely if you lack full pain-free overhead shoulder mobility or have any history of shoulder or neck problems.

bench-calf-stretch.description: A standing stretch with the ball of the foot on a bench edge, dropping the heel to lengthen the calf.
instructions: Place the ball of one foot on the edge of a bench.
Keep that knee straight.
Let your heel drop down below the toes.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hold the bench or a wall for balance.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.

bench-decline-plank-hold.description: A plank with your hands on the floor and your feet on a bench behind you, so that your body slopes downward toward your hands. The raised feet shift more of your weight onto the shoulders and make the abdominal muscles work harder than in a normal plank.
instructions: Place a bench behind you and put the tops of your feet on it, then put your hands on the floor under your shoulders with your arms straight.
Walk your hands to a position where your body is in one straight line from your head to your heels.
Squeeze your glutes, brace your abs and push the floor away so that your shoulders do not sink between your shoulder blades.
Keep your neck in line with your spine and look at the floor between your hands.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly.
Lower your knees to the floor and rest.
tips: Do not let the hips sag or rise above the line; stop the set when the line breaks.
Keep your hands directly under your shoulders so that the weight is carried by the skeleton, not by sore wrists.
Use a lower step if the bench is too high to keep a straight line.

bench-hollow-hold.description: A static core hold performed lying on a flat bench: the arms reach overhead and the shoulders and straight legs are lifted into a shallow hollow shape while the lower back stays pressed into the bench.
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with the glutes and lower back on the pad and the legs extended.
Reach the arms overhead beside the ears.
Brace the abdominals and press the lower back into the bench.
Lift the shoulders and the straight legs a few inches to form a shallow hollow.
Hold the position while breathing steadily, then lower to rest.
tips: If the lower back arches off the pad, raise the legs higher or bend the knees slightly.
Keep the ribs pulled down and the neck relaxed.
Hold only as long as you can keep the lower back flat.

bench-pull.description: A rowing exercise performed lying face down on an elevated bench, eliminating body momentum to target the lats and rhomboids.
instructions: Lie face down on an elevated bench with arms hanging straight down.
Grip a barbell or dumbbells below you.
Row the weight up to the underside of the bench.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your chest glued to the bench to prevent cheating.
Reach a full stretch at the bottom before each pull.
Drive your elbows up and back rather than curling the weight.

bent-over-db-row.description: A two-arm bent-over row with a dumbbell in each hand. The free movement of independent dumbbells lets the elbows track natural and adds a stability demand that a barbell row hides.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, palms facing in.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back until the torso is roughly 30–45 degrees from horizontal, dumbbells hanging directly below the shoulders.
Brace the core and pull both dumbbells up and slightly back, driving the elbows past the ribs.
Squeeze the upper back at the top, keeping the elbows tucked.
Lower under control to the starting position with the arms fully extended.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The torso angle stays fixed throughout — no rocking up to help the dumbbells.
Pull to the lower ribs/belly, not to the chest; that line keeps the lats loaded.
If the lower back rounds, hinge less and reset before the next set.

bird-dog.description: A core stability exercise extending opposite arm and leg to challenge the erector spinae and deep core.
instructions: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Extend your right arm forward and left leg back simultaneously.
Hold for a moment, then return.
Repeat on the other side.
Alternate.
tips: Move slowly and with control.
Keep hips level throughout.

bodyweight-good-morning.description: A bodyweight hip hinge with hands behind the head, strengthening the hamstrings and spinal erectors.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands behind your head.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.
Hinge at the hips and lower your torso toward parallel.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Push your hips back as if closing a door behind you.
Keep your spine neutral from head to tailbone throughout.
Stop the descent when your hamstrings reach their stretch limit.

bodyweight-squat.description: A foundational lower-body exercise squatting with body weight only, developing the quadriceps, glutes, and basic movement mechanics.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended forward.
Sit back and down by bending your hips and knees.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your weight spread across your whole foot.
Track your knees in line with your toes.
Keep your chest up to avoid rounding the upper back.

bulgarian-split-squat.description: A single-leg squat variation with the rear foot elevated.
instructions: Stand in front of a bench, place one foot behind you on the bench.
Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand back up.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Track your front knee over your toes without letting it cave inward.
Square your hips forward and avoid rotating toward the bench.

cable-chest-press.description: A standing chest press on the cable machine, providing constant tension while the staggered stance demands core stability.
instructions: Set the cables to chest height and face away from the machine.
Grip a handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance.
Press the handles forward until your arms are extended.
Squeeze your chest at the top.
Return under control and repeat.
tips: Press both handles evenly to avoid twisting your torso.
Brace your core against the backward pull of the stack.
Step forward enough that the cables stay taut throughout each rep.

cable-fly.description: An isolation movement for the chest using cable resistance for constant tension.
instructions: Stand between two cable columns with handles attached to high pulleys.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms wide.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Maintain the same elbow bend throughout; do not press the weight.
Step one foot forward for a stable, balanced stance.
Control the stretch; do not let the cables yank your arms back.

cable-lateral-raise.description: A unilateral lateral raise on the cable, providing constant tension on the side delt.
instructions: Stand sideways to a low pulley and grip the handle with the hand farther from the machine.
Keep a soft bend in the elbow and let the cable run across the front of your body.
Raise the arm out to the side until parallel to the floor.
Lower under control. Complete reps per side, then switch.
Maintain tension — do not let the weight rest at the bottom.
tips: Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
Pause briefly at the top, do not swing.
Use a lighter load than for dumbbell — cable tension is constant.

cable-reverse-fly.description: A standing cable exercise for the rear deltoids: facing the space between two cable towers, you hold the opposite handles with the cables crossed in front of you and sweep your arms out and back until they are level with your shoulders. The cables keep tension on the back of the shoulders through the whole arc.
instructions: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height and stand centred between the two cable towers.
Take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand, so the cables cross in front of you.
Stand tall with your arms reaching forward at shoulder height and a slight bend in the elbows.
Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc, leading with the elbows, until they are in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly without arching your lower back.
Bring the handles back to the crossed start position slowly and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows soft and fixed; bending and straightening them turns the fly into a row.
Keep your shoulders down and your neck relaxed so the rear deltoids do the work, not the upper trapezius.
Use a light weight and a slow return; the cables pull hardest at the end of the arc, so control that position.

calf-raise-hold.description: An isometric calf exercise: you rise onto the balls of your feet with the knees straight and hold the top position. The gastrocnemius and the soleus stay under constant tension at the point where a calf raise is hardest, with no movement to hide behind.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
Push through the balls of your feet and rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Keep your knees straight and your weight over the middle of your feet, not rolling out to the little toes.
Stop at the top and hold the position, heels as high as possible.
Keep your hips level, your chest tall and your breathing slow while you hold for the planned time.
Lower your heels slowly to the floor and rest.
tips: Hold on to a wall or a rack with one hand if you wobble; the aim is the calf contraction, not the balance.
Do not let the heels sink during the hold; if they drop, end the set instead of bouncing back up.
Add a pair of dumbbells or a loaded backpack once you can hold bodyweight for a full minute.

cat-cow.description: A kneeling flow that alternates between rounding the spine towards the ceiling and letting it sag while the chest opens, moving every segment of the back through its range.
instructions: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Exhale and round the spine towards the ceiling, tucking the tailbone and letting the head drop.
Inhale and reverse it: let the belly sink, lift the chest and tailbone, and look slightly forward.
Move between the two shapes slowly, one breath per position.
Finish in a neutral spine and sit back onto the heels.
tips: Let the breath set the tempo rather than rushing between the two positions.
Keep the hands pressing evenly so the shoulders do not collapse towards the floor.
Move the whole spine, including the neck, instead of hinging only at the lower back.

chest-press-machine.description: A machine-based pressing movement for the chest, ideal for beginners.
instructions: Sit in the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles at chest level.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the pad as you press.
Press to full extension without forcefully locking your elbows.

chest-supported-machine-row.description: A seated rowing machine exercise with a chest pad that supports the torso, so the lats and the muscles between the shoulder blades do the pulling and the lower back stays out of it. You pull the handles back by driving the elbows behind you, then let them return forward with control.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles sit at lower-chest height, then sit with your chest against the pad and your feet planted.
Reach forward and take the handles with your arms extended and your shoulders relaxed.
Brace your trunk, then pull the handles back by driving your elbows behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull without lifting your chest off the pad.
Pause briefly, then extend your arms to return the handles forward under control.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, keeping your chest on the pad throughout.
tips: Pull with the elbows rather than the hands, so the lats and mid-back lead and the biceps assist.
Keep the chest on the pad and the shoulders down; shrugging or leaning back turns the row into an upper trapezius pull.
Let the shoulder blades spread forward at the start of each repetition to get a full stretch before the next pull.

chin-ups.description: A supinated-grip pull-up that strongly activates the biceps alongside the lats.
instructions: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Pull yourself up until chin is above the bar.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep the core tight throughout.
Avoid excessive swinging.

clean.description: An Olympic lift pulling a barbell explosively from the floor to the front-rack position on the shoulders.
instructions: Stand over a loaded barbell with feet hip-width apart.
Grip the bar just outside your knees with an overhand grip.
Drive explosively through your legs and extend your hips.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on your front deltoids.
Stand fully upright to complete the lift.
tips: Keep the bar close to your body as it travels up.
Finish your leg drive fully before pulling under the bar.
Catch with your elbows high so the bar rests on your shoulders.

close-grip-db-bench-press.description: A dumbbell bench press with dumbbells held together to increase triceps involvement.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and hold two dumbbells together over your chest.
Lower them to your chest keeping elbows close.
Press back up.
Repeat.
tips: Press the dumbbells together throughout the movement.
Keep elbows tucked.

close-grip-lat-pulldown.description: A lat pulldown variation using a close, parallel-grip handle to emphasize the lower lats and biceps.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pad.
Grip the close-grip handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Return under control and repeat.
tips: Lean back only slightly, not excessively.
Avoid using momentum to pull the handle down.
Drive your elbows down and back, not just your hands.

cobra-stretch.description: A prone backbend that stretches the abdominals and front of the torso by lifting the chest.
instructions: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders.
Press through your hands to lift your chest off the floor.
Keep your hips and legs on the floor, shoulders relaxed.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your elbows slightly bent — do not force full extension.
Draw your shoulders down away from your ears.

copenhagen-plank.description: A demanding side plank in which the top leg rests on a flat bench and the lower leg is held off the floor. The inner thigh muscles of the top leg and the obliques hold the body in a straight line, which makes it a classic exercise for the adductors and the trunk.
instructions: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place your top leg on it, with the inside of the foot or the lower part of the leg resting on the bench.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top foot, and let the lower leg hang or lift it toward the bench.
Keep your hips high and your trunk steady, and breathe evenly.
Hold for the planned time, then lower your hips back to the floor.
Rest, then switch sides.
tips: Start with the top knee on the bench and a short lever; move the foot of the top leg onto the bench only when the hold feels easy.
Press your forearm into the floor and keep your shoulder away from your ear.
Stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.

crab-dips.description: A floor triceps exercise from the reverse tabletop position: with the hands behind the hips and the trunk lifted, the elbows bend and straighten to move the body up and down.
instructions: Sit with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands on the floor behind you, fingers pointing towards the heels.
Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the trunk is roughly level with the knees.
Bend the elbows straight back to lower the hips towards the floor without sitting down.
Push back up until the arms are straight, keeping the hips lifted.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and lower the hips to finish.
tips: Keep the elbows pointing back, not flaring out to the sides.
Hold the hips high the whole set; letting them drop turns it into a rest.
Walk the feet further away for a longer lever and more triceps work.

cross-body-shoulder-stretch.description: A standing stretch that targets the rear shoulder by drawing one arm horizontally across the chest.
instructions: Stand tall and bring one straight arm across your chest.
Hook your other forearm under it.
Gently pull the arm closer to your chest.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the stretching shoulder down, not shrugged.
Do not pull on the elbow joint itself.

dancer-pose.description: A standing balance on one leg where the free foot is held behind the body and pressed away, combining a backbend with a single-leg hold.
instructions: Stand tall and shift the weight onto one foot, keeping that knee soft.
Bend the other knee and take hold of the inside of that ankle behind you.
Press the lifted foot back into the hand and reach the opposite arm forward as the chest lifts.
Hold the shape for the prescribed time with the standing hip level and the gaze steady.
Release the foot and repeat on the other side.
tips: Fix the eyes on one point ahead; a moving gaze is what usually breaks the balance.
Keep the lifted knee in line with the hip rather than letting it swing out sideways.
Use a strap around the lifted foot if the shoulder does not allow the direct grip.

db-kickstand-deadlift.description: A staggered-stance hip hinge with one dumbbell that loads the front leg while the back foot provides light balance support.
instructions: Step one foot back so only the toes lightly touch the floor, and hinge at the hips with a flat back.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand, low beside the front foot.
Drive through the front heel and extend the hips to stand tall, the dumbbell at your side.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot throughout.
Hinge back down, lowering the dumbbell toward the floor with a flat back. Complete all reps, then switch sides.
tips: Keep the dumbbell close to the shin on the descent.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the front hamstring.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.

db-pullover.description: A compound movement targeting the lats and chest with a stretching motion.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell held above your chest, arms extended.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head in an arc, keeping slight bend in elbows.
Stretch until you feel tension in your lats and chest.
Pull the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Cup one end of the dumbbell with both hands for a secure grip.
Avoid excessive arching in your lower back during the stretch.
Lower only as far as your shoulder mobility comfortably allows.

db-skull-crusher.description: A lying triceps extension with dumbbells allowing independent arm movement.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells over your chest.
Lower the dumbbells toward the sides of your head.
Extend your arms back up.
Repeat.
tips: Keep elbows pointing toward the ceiling.
Use a controlled tempo.

db-sumo-squat.description: A wide-stance squat holding one dumbbell vertically between the legs, biasing the inner thighs and glutes.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out about 30 degrees.
Hold one dumbbell vertically by its top end with both hands, letting it hang between your legs.
Brace the core and keep the chest up.
Bend at the hips and knees to sit straight down into a deep squat.
Drive through the heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Track the knees over the toes — do not let them cave in.
Keep the torso as upright as the hip mobility allows.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down; it should not touch the floor at the bottom.

dead-hang.description: A static hang from a pull-up bar with arms fully extended, primarily challenging grip and forearm strength.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with palms facing away, shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended and feet off the ground.
Relax your shoulders and let your body hang.
Keep your core lightly engaged.
Hold for the desired duration.
tips: Build up your hold time gradually across sessions.
Breathe steadily throughout the hold instead of holding your breath.
Land softly with bent knees when you release the bar.

decline-bench-press-ez-bar.description: A decline press using an EZ-bar for a wrist-friendly grip targeting the lower chest.
instructions: Set the bench to a decline. Secure your feet and grip the EZ-bar.
Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press back up explosively.
Repeat.
tips: The angled grip reduces wrist strain.
Keep your core braced.

deep-squat-hold.description: A static bottom-position squat held with the hips below the knees, the heels flat and the hands clasped in front of the chest. It builds endurance and mobility in the hips, knees and ankles.
instructions: Stand with the feet slightly wider than the shoulders and the toes turned out.
Clasp the hands in front of the chest and sit the hips down between the heels.
Lower until the hips are below the knees while the heels stay flat on the floor.
Keep the chest up and press the elbows against the knees to push them out.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then stand up.
tips: Keep the heels flat; if they lift, place a small plate or wedge under them.
Push the knees out in line with the toes and keep the spine long.
Build the hold time gradually, standing to reset between sets.

dips.description: A compound bodyweight exercise targeting the lower chest and triceps.
instructions: Grip parallel dip bars and lift yourself to the top position with arms locked.
Lean your torso forward slightly.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until shoulders are below elbows.
Press back up to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
Bend your knees and cross your ankles to minimize swinging.
Stop the descent if you feel pinching in your shoulders.

double-db-kickstand-deadlift.description: A staggered-stance hip hinge with two dumbbells that distributes load primarily through the front leg while the back foot lightly grounds for balance.
instructions: Step one foot back so only the toes touch the floor, and hinge at the hips with a flat back.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, low on either side of the front shin.
Drive through the front heel and extend the hips to stand tall, the dumbbells at your sides.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot throughout.
Hinge back down, lowering both dumbbells toward the floor with a flat back. Switch sides after all reps.
tips: Keep the dumbbells close to the legs throughout the movement.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the front hamstring.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.

double-kettlebell-clean-and-press.description: A full-body power exercise that cleans two kettlebells from the floor to the racked position at the shoulders and then presses both overhead to lockout in one continuous sequence.
instructions: Stand with two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, feet about hip-width apart, and hinge at the hips to grip one handle in each hand.
Drive through your legs and extend your hips explosively to pull both kettlebells up, then rotate your elbows under and catch the bells in the racked position at the front of your shoulders.
Brace your core and press both kettlebells overhead until your arms are fully locked out.
Lower the kettlebells back to the racked position, then down to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep the kettlebells close to your body during the clean and punch your hands around and through the handles as you catch them, so the bells settle on your forearms instead of banging into them.
Use a slight dip-drive from the legs and hips to start the press, then finish with the shoulders — keep your core tight so you do not lean back under the load.
At lockout keep your wrists straight and the kettlebells stacked over your elbows and shoulders, with your head returning to a neutral position between the bells.

double-kettlebell-overhead-carry.description: A loaded walk with a kettlebell locked out above each shoulder — the hardest of the carries to keep still, combining the offset mass of the bells with double the overhead load.
instructions: Clean two kettlebells to the rack, then press or push press both to lockout overhead.
Straighten both elbows and settle each bell behind and above its wrist, with your wrists straight.
Pull your ribs down and brace hard before the first step; with both bells overhead there is nothing to counterbalance with.
Walk forward with short, controlled strides, keeping both bells stacked over your shoulders.
Keep looking straight ahead and breathe steadily through the carry.
Cover the desired distance, then lower both bells to the rack and down under control.
tips: Earn this one. Be comfortable with the single-bell overhead carry on both sides before loading two.
Only do it where you can safely drop both bells, and know which way you will step if you have to.
Distance should be short and posture perfect. The moment your back arches or a wrist folds, the set is finished.

double-kettlebell-row.description: A bent-over rowing exercise pulling two kettlebells to the hips, strengthening the lats and upper back.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips.
Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Row both kettlebells to your hips by driving elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Hold your hinge angle steady; avoid standing up as you pull.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing at the floor ahead.
Brace your core to protect your lower back throughout.

downward-dog-knee-tuck.description: A moving core drill held in downward dog: the hips stay high while one knee is drawn in under the chest and sent back to the start, alternating sides. The shoulders support the whole set, so the trunk works without the low-hip position of a plank.
instructions: Set up in downward dog with the hands shoulder-width apart and the hips high.
Press the floor away and brace the trunk so the lower back stays long.
Draw one knee in towards the chest, rounding the upper back slightly as it comes in.
Extend the leg back to the starting position under control.
Repeat with the other leg and keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the hips high; letting them drop turns this into a mountain climber.
Draw the knee in with the abdominals rather than by hopping off the standing foot.
Push the shoulders away from the ears so the upper body does not sink between the arms.

downward-dog-to-plank.description: A moving transition between downward dog and a high plank: the hips travel from high to level and back, so the shoulders and trunk work through a full range instead of holding one position.
instructions: Set up in downward dog with the hips high and the hands shoulder-width apart.
Shift the weight forward and lower the hips until the body forms a straight line in a high plank.
Hold the plank for a moment with the ribs down and the glutes engaged.
Press the floor away and lift the hips back up into downward dog.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move the hips, not the hands; the palms stay in the same place the whole set.
Keep the shoulders pushing away from the ears in both positions.
Slow the transition down if the lower back sags on the way into the plank.

dumbbell-bench-pull.description: A prone rowing movement on a bench for strict upper back work.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench holding dumbbells.
Let your arms hang straight down.
Pull the dumbbells up toward your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your chest glued to the bench throughout the pull.
Drive your elbows up and back rather than curling the weight.
Let your shoulder blades protract fully at the bottom for full range.

dumbbell-deadlift.description: A deadlift variation using a pair of dumbbells, training the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, hinge at the hips with a flat back and hold the dumbbells low, at shin height.
Brace your core and keep the dumbbells close to your legs.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips to stand up tall.
Extend your hips fully at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
Hinge back down, lowering the dumbbells along your legs to your shins.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Brace your core before each rep to keep your spine stable.
Balance your weight over midfoot rather than your toes.
Keep your neck in line with your spine rather than looking up.

dumbbell-front-raise.description: An isolation exercise targeting the anterior deltoid through a forward raise motion.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Raise one or both dumbbells forward to shoulder height.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid using momentum.
Slight elbow bend reduces joint stress.

dumbbell-push-press.description: A compound overhead press that uses a leg drive to initiate momentum and develop shoulder and triceps power.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Slightly bend your knees into a quarter squat.
Drive through your legs to generate momentum, then press the dumbbells overhead.
Lock out your arms at the top.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control.
tips: Use a shallow dip — this is not a full squat.
Drive the heels into the floor to initiate the press.
Keep your core braced to protect the lower back.

dumbbell-side-bend.description: A standing oblique isolation exercise using a dumbbell to develop lateral core strength and stability.
instructions: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
Keep the opposite hand on your hip or behind your head.
Bend laterally toward the dumbbell side, lowering it along your thigh.
Return to upright, then bend to the opposite side using only your obliques.
Complete all reps per side.
tips: Avoid leaning forward or backward — move strictly sideways.
Use a controlled tempo in both directions.
Keep the weight close to your leg throughout.

dumbbell-upright-row.description: A compound pulling movement with dumbbells that targets the lateral deltoids and upper trapezius.
instructions: Stand holding two dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Pull the dumbbells straight up along your body, leading with your elbows.
Raise until the dumbbells reach chin height and elbows are above the wrists.
Pause briefly, then lower with control.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Keep the dumbbells close to your body throughout.
Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Avoid pulling with a very narrow grip to reduce shoulder impingement risk.

easy-pose.description: A simple cross-legged seat used for breathing and meditation: the pelvis stays upright, the spine is tall and the hips settle without strain.
instructions: Sit on the floor and cross the shins comfortably, each foot under the opposite knee.
Sit up on a folded blanket or cushion until the knees rest below the level of the hips.
Stack the ribs over the pelvis and let the hands rest on the thighs.
Hold the seat for the prescribed time, breathing slowly and evenly.
Switch which shin is in front on the next round so both sides get equal time.
tips: If the knees float high, raise the seat rather than forcing them down.
Let the chin stay level so the neck follows the line of the spine.
Support the knees on cushions when a long sit gets uncomfortable.

ez-bar-curl.description: An isolation exercise targeting the biceps using an EZ-bar, which reduces wrist strain compared to a straight barbell.
instructions: Stand holding an EZ-bar with an underhand grip on the angled portions.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows pinned.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Use the inner or outer grip to vary emphasis.
Keep your wrists neutral on the angled grips.

ez-bar-pullover.description: This compound exercise targets the lats and pectorals by extending the arms overhead with an EZ bar, promoting upper body strength and hypertrophy.
instructions: Lie supine on a flat bench with your head slightly off the end, holding an EZ bar with a pronated grip.
Extend the bar straight above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the bar in an arc behind your head, feeling a stretch in your lats and chest.
Pull the bar back to the starting position using your lats and pectorals.
Maintain control throughout the movement, avoiding momentum.
tips: Keep your core braced to prevent arching your lower back excessively.
Focus on a deep stretch at the bottom of the movement.
Use a spotter for heavier loads to ensure safety.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase for maximum muscle engagement.

ez-bar-shrug.description: A shrug using an EZ-bar for a comfortable grip while loading the trapezius.
instructions: Stand holding an EZ-bar in front of you.
Shrug your shoulders straight up.
Hold at the top, then lower.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid rolling the shoulders in circles.
Use a full range of motion.

face-pull.description: A cable exercise targeting the rear deltoids and external rotators.
instructions: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends.
Squeeze your rear deltoids and external rotators.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows high, roughly in line with your shoulders.
Choose a light weight and prioritize control over load.
Avoid leaning back or shrugging your shoulders as you pull.

floor-ez-bar-press.description: A floor press variation using an EZ-bar for a more comfortable wrist and elbow position.
instructions: Lie on the floor holding an EZ-bar over your chest.
Lower the bar until your elbows touch the floor.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: The EZ-bar reduces wrist strain vs. a straight bar.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.

frog-stretch.description: A floor stretch for the inner thighs and groin: on your hands and knees, you slide the knees wide apart with the feet turned out and rock your hips back toward your heels. The wide knees open the adductors while the hips stay low.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees on the floor, with your wrists under your shoulders.
Slide your knees out to the sides as far as is comfortable and turn your feet out, keeping your shins in line with your knees.
Lower onto your forearms and keep your back straight, not rounded.
Rock your hips back toward your heels until you feel a strong stretch along your inner thighs.
Hold the position and breathe slowly, keeping your hips level.
Come out by sliding the knees together and sitting back before you stand.
tips: Put a folded towel or mat under your knees if the floor is hard.
Go only as wide as you can keep your hips level; letting the pelvis tilt takes the stretch out of the inner thighs.
Rock back slowly and ease out of the position if you feel any pinching at the front of the hips.

glute-bridge.description: A bodyweight glute activation exercise performed lying on the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes.
Hold briefly at the top with hips fully extended.
Lower your hips back down with control.
Repeat.
tips: Push through your heels rather than your toes.
Avoid arching your lower back at the top.
Don't let your knees cave inward as you lift.

goblet-squat.description: A beginner-friendly squat with a kettlebell held at chest height for improved posture and depth.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Squat down keeping the weight close to your chest.
Drive back up.
Repeat.
tips: The goblet position naturally encourages an upright torso.
Push knees out at the bottom.

half-kneeling-hip-flexor-rock.description: The dynamic version of the kneeling hip-flexor stretch: from a half-kneeling stance the hips rock forward into the stretch and back out of it, repeated instead of held.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you.
Tuck the tailbone slightly and brace the trunk so the lower back stays neutral.
Rock the hips forward until you feel the front of the back thigh lengthen.
Rock back out of the position under control and repeat rhythmically.
Switch sides and repeat for the same number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the movement in the hips; if the lower back arches, shorten the range.
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg during the forward rock.
Pad the down knee with a folded mat if the floor is hard.

handstand-push-ups.description: An inverted press in a freestanding handstand on parallettes, lowering the head between the handles and pressing back up to straight arms.
instructions: Set two parallettes shoulder-width apart and kick up into a freestanding handstand on them.
Brace your core and keep your body straight, legs together.
Bend your elbows to lower your head between the handles.
Go down until your head is about level with the handles.
Press through the handles back to straight arms, keeping your balance.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lower under control instead of dropping into the bottom position.
Keep the ribs down and the body stacked over the hands so the back does not arch.
Learn it against a wall and through pike push-ups before going freestanding.

hanging-knee-raise.description: A hanging core exercise on a pull-up bar that targets the lower abs and hip flexors with bent knees.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
Engage your core and raise your knees toward your chest.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower your legs slowly back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Avoid swinging — initiate the movement from your core.
Exhale as you raise your knees.
Progress to straight-leg raises when this feels easy.

hanging-tuck-hold.description: A static core hold hanging from a bar with the knees pulled up toward the chest. It trains the abdominals and hip flexors and is a step toward the hanging L-sit.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and the arms straight.
Brace the abdominals and pull the knees up toward the chest, rounding the lower back slightly.
Keep the knees together and the thighs at or above hip height.
Hold the tucked position without swinging and breathe steadily.
Lower the legs under control to a full hang.
tips: Curl the pelvis up rather than just lifting the knees; the abdominals should do the work.
Keep the shoulders pulled away from the ears.
End the set when the knees start to drop or the body starts to swing.

heel-flicks.description: A running warm-up drill that alternates the heels towards the glutes, raising the cadence while dynamically flexing the knees and preparing the hamstrings.
instructions: Stand tall with the feet under the hips and the arms bent as for running.
Begin jogging lightly in place.
Flick one heel up towards the same-side glute without driving the knee forward.
Switch feet quickly and continue alternating at an even rhythm.
Stay light on the forefeet and keep the torso upright for the full interval.
tips: Aim for quick relaxed contacts rather than forcing the heel into the glute.
Keep the knees pointing down instead of lifting them like high knees.
Start slowly and increase cadence only after the rhythm feels smooth.

hex-bar-deadlift.description: A deadlift standing inside a hex (trap) bar, keeping the load centered for a more upright, back-friendly pull.
instructions: Stand inside a loaded trap bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and knees to grip the handles.
Brace your core and set your back flat.
Drive through your heels and extend hips and knees to stand up.
Lock out at the top with shoulders pulled back.
Lower the bar back to the floor under control.
tips: Keep your chest up and back flat as you set your grip.
Push the floor away rather than yanking the bar with your back.
Stand fully upright at the top without leaning back.

hip-abduction.description: A machine exercise targeting the outer hip muscles.
instructions: Sit in the hip abduction machine with pads against your outer thighs.
Push your legs apart against the resistance.
Hold briefly at the widest point.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat.
tips: Sit tall and keep your back against the pad.
Don't let the weight stack slam down between reps.
Choose a resistance that allows a full range of motion.

horizontal-leg-press.description: A machine leg press performed horizontally, targeting quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Sit in a horizontal leg press with your back against the pad and your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate.
Press through your feet to straighten your legs, stopping just short of locking the knees.
Bend your knees under control until they come toward your chest.
Repeat.
tips: Do not let your lower back lift off the seat.
Avoid locking out the knees completely.

incline-bench-ez-bar-press.description: An incline press with an EZ-bar targeting the upper chest with a joint-friendly grip.
instructions: Set bench to 30–45 degrees. Grip the EZ-bar with hands on the angled sections.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: The incline shifts emphasis to the upper pectorals.
Control the descent to avoid shoulder strain.

incline-dumbbell-fly.description: An incline isolation exercise opening dumbbells in a wide arc, stretching and targeting the upper chest.
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench holding dumbbells above your chest.
Press the dumbbells up with palms facing each other.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower the dumbbells in a wide arc until you feel a chest stretch.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower only as far as a comfortable chest stretch allows.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together.

incline-treadmill-walk.description: A steady uphill walk on an inclined treadmill belt, keeping one foot in contact with the belt throughout so the glutes and hamstrings work hard with almost no impact.
instructions: Start the belt at a slow walking speed and step on, then raise the incline to your target gradient.
Walk with a long, deliberate stride, rolling from heel to toe and pushing the belt away behind you with each step.
Stand tall and lean from the ankles with the hill rather than folding forward at the waist.
Keep at least one foot on the belt at all times — walk the hill, do not break into a jog.
Let your arms swing naturally, or rest them lightly on the rails for balance without carrying your weight on them.
Hold the gradient for the desired time, then lower the incline and walk level for a few minutes to finish.
tips: Pick a speed you can still walk at. As soon as you need a flight phase to keep up, drop the speed or the incline — it is a walk, not a run.
Hanging your bodyweight off the handrails removes most of the work the hill is there to create; touch them for balance only.
The steep grade is what moves the effort from the quads into the glutes and hamstrings, so raise the incline before you raise the speed.

jackknife-sit-up.description: A full-body crunch performed lying on the floor, lifting both legs and torso simultaneously to touch hands to feet.
instructions: Lie face-up on the floor with arms extended overhead and legs extended straight.
Simultaneously lift the torso and the straight legs off the floor.
Reach the hands up toward the feet as the feet rise — meet above the hips.
Lower the torso and legs back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Arms and legs move at the same speed — avoid a kick-first cheat.
If the lower back arches on the return, slow down and don't fully touch the floor.

jumping-jacks.description: This classic full-body dynamic exercise elevates heart rate and targets the calves, shoulders, quads, and glutes, making it an excellent warm-up or conditioning movement.
instructions: Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
Simultaneously jump your feet out wide and raise your arms overhead.
Ensure your arms meet or nearly meet above your head.
Jump your feet back together while lowering your arms to your sides.
Maintain a continuous, rhythmic motion.
tips: Land softly on the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
Control your breathing; inhale as you jump out, exhale as you jump in.
Increase speed for a greater cardiovascular challenge.

kettlebell-close-grip-floor-press.description: A floor press performed with a single kettlebell gripped close together with both hands. The narrow grip and the floor stop on the elbows shift emphasis off the chest and onto the triceps, with no shoulder hyperextension.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with the knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a single kettlebell by the handle with both hands, close together, the bell resting on the chest with elbows tucked tight to the ribs.
Brace the core and press the kettlebell straight up until the arms are fully extended.
Lower under control until the upper arms touch the floor and pause briefly.
Press back up to lockout.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows tucked at roughly 30–45 degrees from the torso — wide elbows turn it into a chest press.
The brief pause when the elbows touch the floor kills the bounce and forces a clean concentric.
Pick a bell you can control with two hands; the narrow grip is unforgiving if it tips.

kettlebell-deadlift.description: A foundational hip-hinge pull lifting a kettlebell from the floor, training the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and kettlebell between your feet.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the handle.
Brace your core and set your back flat.
Drive through your heels to stand up with the kettlebell.
Lock out at the top with shoulders pulled back.
Lower the kettlebell back to the floor with control.
tips: Keep the kettlebell close to your shins as you lift.
Think of pushing the floor away rather than lifting with your back.
Look at a spot on the floor ahead to keep your neck neutral.

kettlebell-halo.description: A shoulder-mobility drill where a kettlebell is circled around the head. Warms up the rotator cuff, thoracic spine, and shoulder girdle with minimal load.
instructions: Stand tall, core braced, holding a light kettlebell by the horns (upside down) at chest height.
Raise the bell to one side of your head and pass it around the back in a smooth circle.
Bring it back to the starting position in front of your face.
Reverse direction every few reps.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions or time.
tips: Light weight only — this is mobility, not strength.
Keep the head stationary; the bell goes around, not the head.
If the bell drifts wide, shrink the circle — tight orbit, close to the skull.

kettlebell-lunge-press.description: A combination exercise pressing a kettlebell overhead with one arm while lunging, training legs, shoulders, and core.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell at shoulder height with one arm.
Step forward into a lunge with the opposite leg.
As you lunge, press the kettlebell overhead.
Lock out the arm at the top of the press.
Step back to standing while lowering the kettlebell.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Brace your core to resist leaning toward the loaded side.
Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes.
Avoid arching your back as you lock out overhead.

kettlebell-overhead-tricep-extension.description: An overhead tricep extension holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands. The offset load pulls the bell behind the head for a deep long-head stretch.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a kettlebell by the horns (upside down) with both hands overhead.
Arms fully extended, bell above the head.
Bend only the elbows to lower the bell behind the head in a controlled arc.
Keep the upper arms vertical and close to the head; only the forearms move.
Extend the elbows to return the bell overhead.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Grip the horns firmly — the bell wants to rotate at the bottom.
Elbows stay narrow; if they flare, drop the load.
A seated version on a bench with a back rest is easier on the lumbar.

kettlebell-reverse-lunge.description: This compound unilateral exercise builds lower body strength and stability, primarily targeting the glutes and quads while engaging hamstrings, glute medius, and obliques.
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the horns at your chest, elbows tucked in (goblet hold).
Step one leg straight back, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Keep your front shin vertical and your chest upright, ensuring your back knee hovers just above the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Complete all reps per side before switching to the other side.
tips: Maintain a stable core throughout the movement to protect your spine.
Focus on a controlled descent and a powerful ascent.
Keep your front foot flat and distribute weight evenly through the heel and midfoot.
Avoid letting your front knee collapse inward; keep it tracking over your toes.

kettlebell-shrug.description: This isolation exercise targets the upper trapezius muscles by elevating the shoulders, enhancing shoulder stability and neck strength.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with palms facing your body.
Keep your arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
Elevate your shoulders straight up towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top.
Hold the contraction briefly.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on moving only your shoulders, keeping your arms straight throughout the movement.
Avoid rolling your shoulders; move them straight up and down.
Maintain a neutral spine and engaged core to prevent lower back strain.
Use a weight that allows for full range of motion and controlled execution.

kettlebell-sumo-deadlift.description: A wide-stance deadlift with a single kettlebell between the feet. The wide stance and close-to-body load make this a quad-and-glute-dominant pattern that is easy to learn.
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with toes pointed slightly out, a kettlebell on the floor between the feet.
Hinge down with a flat back, knees tracking over the toes, and grip the handle with both hands.
Drive through the floor and extend the hips and knees together to stand up.
Squeeze the glutes at the top.
Lower the bell under control back to the floor by pushing the hips back.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Knees track out over the toes — do not let them cave in.
Shoulders stay above the hips at the bottom; if the shoulders drop, narrow the stance.
Keep the bell close to the body throughout the lift.

kettlebell-swing-clean.description: A hip-driven clean swinging the kettlebell from between the legs up to the shoulder rack position.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell between your feet.
Hinge at the hips and grip the handle with one hand.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to pull the kettlebell up to your shoulder.
Catch the kettlebell in the rack position on your shoulder.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep the kettlebell close to your body on the way up.
Let the kettlebell roll around your wrist rather than flipping over it.
Relax your grip slightly at the top for a soft catch.

kettlebell-wrist-curl.description: A wrist curl with a kettlebell in each hand, with the offset weight adding extra grip challenge.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forearms on your thighs, palms up.
Hold a kettlebell by the handle in each hand, with the wrists hanging off the knees.
Let the kettlebells rotate down toward the fingertips.
Curl them up by flexing the wrists, controlling the offset weight.
Lower under control and repeat for the planned reps.
tips: Hold the handles, not the bells, so the offset weight loads the grip.
Move only at the wrists.
Use a lighter load than you would for a dumbbell.

kneeling-hip-flexor-stretch.description: A half-kneeling stretch that opens the hip flexors of the rear leg by pressing the hips forward.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front.
Keep your torso upright and core gently braced.
Press your hips forward until the front of the rear hip stretches.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg to protect the lower back.
Avoid arching your lower back.

landmine-single-arm-overhead-hold.description: A one-arm isometric hold at the top of the landmine press: you press the end of the barbell overhead and stay locked out. The shoulder, the chest and the serratus keep the bar steady while the trunk resists the sideways pull of the angled bar.
instructions: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine post or in a corner and stand facing the free end in a staggered stance, feet about shoulder-width apart.
Hold the end of the bar with one hand at the shoulder and keep your other hand on your hip.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight and your hand is above and slightly in front of your shoulder.
Lock out your elbow and push your shoulder blade around your ribs without shrugging.
Hold the bar steady for the planned time, with your trunk braced so that you do not lean to the side.
Lower the bar to your shoulder under control and switch arms.
tips: Keep the ribs down and the glutes squeezed so that you do not arch your lower back as you hold.
Push the shoulder away from your ear at the top; do not let it shrug up toward your neck.
Use a lighter load than for the press; holding for time is harder than a single repetition.

lean-back-90-90-hold.description: A gentler version of the 90/90 hip hold: from the same 90/90 leg position, you lean your trunk back and support it on your hands behind you. Leaning back takes some load off the hips while keeping the front leg turned out and the back leg turned in.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your front leg bent in front of you to about 90 degrees and your back leg out to the side, also bent to about 90 degrees.
Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing back or to the side.
Lean your trunk back onto your hands, keeping your arms straight and your chest open.
Let both knees settle toward the floor without forcing them.
Hold the position, breathing slowly, feeling a mild stretch in the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the hip of the back leg.
Hold for the planned time, then switch the legs and hold on the other side.
tips: Use this version when the upright 90/90 is too intense; lean further back on your hands to ease the stretch.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears rather than hanging on your arms.
Move slowly into the position and keep it pain-free, especially at the knees.

leg-swing-front-to-back.description: A dynamic hip-mobility drill that swings one straight or softly bent leg forwards and backwards while the standing side stabilises the pelvis.
instructions: Stand tall beside a stable support and shift the weight onto the inside leg.
Brace the trunk and lift the outside foot slightly from the floor.
Swing the free leg forwards through a comfortable range.
Let it travel back behind the body without arching the lower back.
Continue smoothly, then repeat with the other leg.
tips: Keep the torso tall and let the movement come from the hip.
Use a small range first and increase it as the hip warms up.
Keep the standing foot planted and the pelvis facing forward.

low-lunge.description: A kneeling split-stance stretch: the back knee rests on the floor while the hips sink forward, lengthening the hip flexor of the rear leg.
instructions: From kneeling, step one foot forward so the knee stacks over the ankle.
Lower the back knee to the floor and untuck that foot.
Tuck the tailbone slightly and press the hips forward until you feel the front of the back thigh lengthen.
Lift the chest, raise the arms if it feels good, and hold for the prescribed time.
Step back and repeat on the other side.
tips: Pad the back knee with a folded mat if the floor is hard.
Squeeze the back glute to deepen the stretch without arching the lower back.
Keep the front knee above the ankle rather than letting it slide forward.

lying-quad-stretch.description: A floor stretch for the front of the thigh: lying on your side, you bend the top knee and pull the heel toward your glute with your hand. Lying down takes balance out of the stretch, so you can relax and let the quadriceps lengthen.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs straight and your head resting on your lower arm.
Bend your top knee and take hold of that foot or ankle with your top hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute, keeping your knees close together.
Tuck your pelvis slightly so your lower back does not arch.
Hold the stretch for the planned time while breathing slowly.
Release the foot, roll to the other side and repeat.
tips: Keep the knees side by side; letting the top knee drift forward turns it into a hip stretch.
Do not pull the heel hard; ease into a stretch you feel in the front of the thigh, not in the knee.
If you cannot reach the foot, loop a towel or strap around the ankle and pull on that.

machine-calf-raise.description: A standing machine exercise isolating the calves through a full stretch and rise onto the toes.
instructions: Stand in the calf raise machine with the balls of your feet on the platform.
Position the shoulder pads firmly.
Lower your heels below the platform for a full stretch.
Push through the balls of your feet to rise onto your toes.
Squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees straight but not locked throughout the movement.
Pause briefly in the stretched position instead of bouncing.
Avoid cutting the range of motion short as fatigue sets in.

machine-seated-crunch.description: An abdominal isolation exercise performed on a seated machine that flexes the spine against resistance.
instructions: Sit in the abdominal crunch machine and grip the handles.
Position the chest pad against your upper body.
Contract your abs to crunch your torso forward and down.
Squeeze at the bottom of the movement.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Initiate the movement with your abs, not your arms.
Exhale as you crunch forward.
Avoid using momentum by rocking your body.

medicine-ball-slam.description: An explosive full-body exercise where a soft slam ball is lifted overhead and driven into the floor with maximum force.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a slam ball in front of your hips.
Lift the ball overhead by extending the hips and reaching tall.
Forcefully slam the ball into the floor between your feet, crunching through the core.
Catch the ball on the bounce or pick it up from the floor.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Use a dead-bounce slam ball, not a traditional medicine ball — regular balls will bounce back into your face.
Finish with the whole body — it is a full swing, not just an arm throw.

muscle-ups.description: An advanced bar movement combining an explosive pull-up with a dip transition to finish above the bar.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a false grip.
Pull yourself up explosively toward the bar.
As your chest reaches the bar, rotate your elbows over and transition into a dip.
Press your body up until your arms are fully extended above the bar.
Lower back down with control through the same path.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use a false grip so your wrists are already over the bar for the transition.
Pull explosively toward your sternum, not just your chin.
Drill the transition on low rings or with bands before full reps.

nordic-hamstring-curl.description: A knee-flexion exercise lowering the torso forward from a kneeling position, working the hamstrings eccentrically.
instructions: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored under a fixed support.
Keep your torso upright and your hips extended.
Slowly lower your body forward by resisting with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands just before hitting the floor.
Push back up and pull yourself to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lower as slowly as possible — the eccentric is the point.
Keep your hips extended; do not fold at the waist.
Catch yourself with your hands and push off lightly while building strength.

one-arm-dumbbell-shoulder-press.description: A standing overhead press performed with a single dumbbell. Working one side at a time loads the shoulder and triceps and makes the trunk resist leaning toward the empty hand.
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell at one shoulder with the palm facing forward.
Brace the abdominals and keep the free arm relaxed at your side.
Press the dumbbell straight overhead until the arm is fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top with the upper arm next to the ear.
Lower the dumbbell back to the shoulder under control.
Complete the repetitions on one arm, then switch sides.
tips: Keep the ribs down and the glutes tight; do not lean sideways to push the weight up.
Press in a straight line close to the head, not out in front.
Start lighter than you would with two dumbbells; the trunk has to stabilise the load.

one-arm-kettlebell-floor-glute-bridge-pr.description: A combined glute bridge and single-arm floor press, training the glutes and chest in one movement.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand at your shoulder.
Drive your hips up into a glute bridge.
Press the kettlebell straight up toward the ceiling.
Lower the kettlebell and your hips with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Hold the bridge steady at the top while pressing.
Keep your wrist straight and stacked under the kettlebell.
Extend your free arm along the floor for extra stability.

one-arm-kettlebell-row.description: A unilateral rowing exercise with bench support, building the lats and mid-back one side at a time.
instructions: Place one hand and knee on a bench for support.
Hold a kettlebell in the opposite hand with your arm extended.
Pull the kettlebell toward your hip by driving your elbow back.
Squeeze your back at the top of the movement.
Lower the kettlebell with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep your torso square to the floor throughout the set.
Pull with your back muscles rather than just your arm.
Keep your neck neutral, eyes on the floor just ahead.

one-arm-landmine-press.description: A unilateral overhead press variation using a landmine setup that follows a natural arc, reducing shoulder impingement risk while building pressing strength.
instructions: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment and load the free end.
Kneel on one knee or stand and grip the sleeve end at shoulder height with one hand.
