Press the bar upward and forward along its arc until the arm is fully extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder height under control.
Complete all reps before switching sides.
tips: Engage your core to prevent the torso from rotating toward the working arm.
The arc motion is more joint-friendly than a vertical overhead press.
Kneeling on the knee on the same side as the pressing arm, with the other foot planted in front, increases the core's anti-rotation demand.

one-arm-single-leg-kettlebell-romanian-d.description: The kettlebell version of the one-arm single-leg RDL. The offset mass of the kettlebell and the lower hanging centre make this a subtly different challenge to the dumbbell variant — excellent for posterior-chain strength and balance under asymmetric load.
instructions: Stand on one leg holding a kettlebell in the opposite hand by the handle.
Free arm out to the side for balance, free leg hovering behind.
Hinge at the standing hip, pushing it back while the free leg extends to counterbalance.
Keep hips square to the floor; the kettlebell tracks straight down the shin.
Feel a deep hamstring stretch on the standing leg at the bottom.
Drive the hip forward to return to standing.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
tips: The kettlebell hangs lower than a dumbbell — shorten the ROM slightly to keep the back flat.
If the bell swings, you are moving too fast. Slow the eccentric.
Build up from the two-arm (dumbbell) single-leg RDL first.

pause-deadlift.description: A deadlift variation with a deliberate pause just above the knees, building strength and position through the upper half of the pull.
instructions: Set up for a conventional deadlift.
Pull the bar off the floor and pause when it passes your knees.
Hold for 2–3 seconds, then complete the lift.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: The pause removes momentum and builds strength and control from the knees to lockout.
Keep your back flat during the pause.

paused-incline-bench-press.description: An incline bench press with a pause on the upper chest, emphasizing strict control and upper-pec strength.
instructions: Lie on an incline bench and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your upper chest.
Pause on your chest for 1-2 seconds.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows during the pause.
Maintain full-body tension while the bar rests on your chest.
Avoid bouncing the bar off your chest after the pause.

pigeon-stretch.description: A seated floor stretch that targets the glutes and outer hip with the front shin folded across the body.
instructions: From all fours, bring one knee forward and lay the shin across in front.
Extend the other leg straight back, top of the foot down.
Sink your hips toward the floor and keep them square.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Place a cushion under the hip if it does not reach the floor.
Walk your hands forward to deepen the stretch.

pilates-leg-pull-front.description: A high plank with alternating leg lifts: the shoulders stay stacked over the wrists while one leg at a time lifts, adding an anti-rotation demand to the plank.
instructions: Set up in a high plank with the hands under the shoulders and the body in one line.
Brace the trunk and squeeze the glutes so the hips cannot rotate.
Lift one straight leg a few centimetres above hip height without letting the pelvis tilt.
Lower it under control and repeat with the other leg.
Keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lift the leg from the glute rather than by arching the lower back.
Keep the weight even in both hands; the tendency is to lean away from the lifted side.
Reduce the lift height until the hips stay perfectly level.

pilates-side-bend.description: A lateral trunk exercise from a side-supported position: the hips lift and the top arm reaches overhead, bending the body sideways over the supporting arm.
instructions: Sit on one hip with the legs bent to the side and the supporting hand on the floor under the shoulder.
Press into the hand and the lower leg to lift the hips off the floor.
Reach the top arm overhead so the body forms a long arc from the hand to the feet.
Lower the hips under control back towards the mat.
Complete the repetitions and change sides.
tips: Push the floor away so the supporting shoulder stays stacked and stable.
Reach the top arm long rather than collapsing sideways.
Keep the movement smooth; the lift and the lower take the same time.

planche.description: An advanced calisthenics hold requiring exceptional upper body and core strength to hold the body parallel to the ground.
instructions: Begin in a push-up position with your hands turned outward on the floor, or on parallettes.
Lean forward until your center of mass is over your hands.
Lift your feet off the ground keeping the body horizontal.
Hold the position.
Return to the floor with control.
tips: Progress through tuck, straddle, and full planche.
Build wrist and shoulder strength before attempting.

plate-loaded-donkey-calf-raise.description: A donkey calf raise on a plate-loaded machine, with a pad across the hips and the torso hinged forward so the calves are stretched at the bottom of every repetition.
instructions: Load the plate horns and step onto the platform with the balls of your feet on the edge and your heels hanging free.
Bend forward at the hips and settle the pad across your hips, then rest your forearms on the support in front of you.
Keep your knees straight and your back flat, with your torso close to parallel to the floor.
Push through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as you can, pausing briefly at the top.
Lower your heels below the platform until you feel a strong calf stretch, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: The forward hinge is the exercise. Standing up straight turns this into an ordinary standing calf raise and gives away the extra stretch you came for.
Keep the knees straight throughout. Bending them shifts the work from the gastrocnemius to the soleus, which is the seated calf raise, not this one.
Let the heels drop all the way below the platform edge. The bottom of the range is where this machine earns its place, and cutting it short wastes the setup.

plate-loaded-shrug.description: A standing shrug on a plate-loaded machine, lifting handles that hang at your sides so the traps work without a bar in front of or behind the legs.
instructions: Load the plate horns evenly and stand on the machine platform, facing away from the frame.
Take a handle in each hand with your arms hanging straight down at your sides and your shoulders relaxed.
Stand tall with your chest up, your chin level and your knees soft.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as they will go, and hold for a moment at the top.
Lower under control until your shoulders are fully down, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Shrug straight up. Rolling the shoulders adds travel but no extra trap work, and it takes the shoulder joint through a loaded circle for nothing.
Keep the arms straight and passive. Bending the elbows turns the movement into a short upright row and takes the load off the traps.
The handles hanging at your sides are what this machine is for -- there is no bar to clear your thighs, so you can stand upright and use a full range without shortening the top.

plyo-lunge.description: An explosive split-stance jump that switches the legs in mid-air, alternating each rep.
instructions: Start in a forward lunge with one foot ahead of the other.
Drop into a deep lunge with the back knee almost touching the floor.
Drive both feet off the floor, switching legs in mid-air.
Land softly in a lunge with the opposite leg forward.
Continue alternating without pausing.
tips: Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
Switch the leg position fully — do not just hop in place.
Keep the torso upright — do not pitch forward.

pseudo-planche-push-ups.description: A push-up with hands turned back and shoulders leaned far past the wrists, mimicking planche loading.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands turned so fingers point back.
Lean your shoulders forward past your wrists.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Keep your body in a straight line.
Press back up while maintaining the forward lean.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: The further you lean forward, the harder each rep becomes.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lower.
Keep your shoulder blades protracted and your body rigid.

push-press.description: A barbell overhead press using leg drive to press heavier loads overhead.
instructions: Stand with a barbell racked on your front deltoids.
Dip slightly at the knees.
Drive up with your legs and press the bar overhead.
Lock out fully.
Lower to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Use leg drive only to initiate — finish with the shoulders.
Keep the core braced throughout.

rear-delt-fly.description: An isolation movement targeting the posterior deltoids and upper back.
instructions: Hold dumbbells and hinge forward at the hips.
With a slight bend in elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Choose a light weight to keep the movement strict.
Avoid using momentum from the torso to swing the weights up.
Lead with your elbows rather than your hands.

reverse-curl.description: A barbell curl with an overhand grip targeting the brachialis and forearm extensors.
instructions: Stand and hold a barbell with an overhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep wrists straight.
Move through a full range of motion.

reverse-nordic-curl.description: A bodyweight quadriceps exercise performed kneeling, leaning the torso backward under control while keeping the hips extended.
instructions: Kneel on a pad with your knees hip-width apart, shins and the tops of your feet on the floor, and your torso upright.
Keep your hips extended and core braced.
Slowly lean your torso backward while keeping your body in a straight line.
Lower as far as you can control with your quadriceps.
Pull yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your hips extended throughout — don't let them fold.
Lower only as far as you can control.
Use a pad under the knees for comfort.

reverse-tabletop-hold.description: A static reverse tabletop: knees bent, hands under the shoulders behind the body, hips lifted level with the knees and held, so the glutes and the whole back of the trunk work isometrically.
instructions: Sit with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands on the floor behind you, fingers pointing towards the heels.
Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the trunk is level with the knees.
Open the chest, draw the shoulders away from the ears and look straight ahead.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the hips high.
Lower the hips under control to finish.
tips: Push the floor away rather than hanging on the shoulders.
Keep the knees stacked over the ankles and pointing straight ahead.
Let the head follow the line of the spine instead of dropping it back.

ring-dips.description: A challenging bodyweight dip performed on gymnastic rings, demanding greater stabilization than bar dips.
instructions: Support yourself on the rings with arms locked out.
Lower your body by bending the elbows until upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Press back up to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Keep the rings close to your body.
Turn the rings out at the top for additional chest activation.

ring-plank.description: A plank held with the hands in gymnastic rings and the feet on the floor. The rings move freely, so the shoulders and trunk have to work harder to keep the body in a straight line.
instructions: Set the rings at about knee height and take hold of them with the arms straight under the shoulders.
Step the feet back into a plank, with the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace the abdominals and glutes and press the rings down and slightly out to keep them steady.
Hold the position without letting the hips sag or the rings drift apart.
Step the feet in and stand up to finish.
tips: Keep the rings directly under the shoulders; if they swing, place the feet wider.
Push the floor away through the rings so the shoulder blades stay wide.
Raise the rings to make the hold easier and lower them to make it harder.

rings-inverted-row.description: A bodyweight row on gymnastic rings hung low, pulling the chest up to the rings from a straight, inclined body line; more challenging than a standing ring row.
instructions: Set the rings just above hip height.
Lie under the rings and grip them with palms facing each other.
Walk the feet forward so the body forms a straight line.
Pull the chest toward the rings, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Lower under control to a full-arm extension.
tips: Keep the body in a straight line — heels through head.
Squeeze the glutes and core to prevent sagging.
Elevate the feet on a box for a harder version.

running.description: Unaided running over ground, with a flight phase in every stride where neither foot is down — the impact and the effort that separates it from walking.
instructions: Start from an easy jog and build into your pace over the first few minutes rather than setting off at target speed.
Land with your foot under your hips, not out in front, and keep the contact with the ground short and quiet.
Run tall through the hips with a slight forward lean from the ankles, not a fold at the waist.
Bend your elbows to about ninety degrees and drive your arms forward and back, keeping them off your chest.
Breathe rhythmically and keep your shoulders, jaw and hands loose.
Hold the pace for the desired time or distance, then jog and walk for a few minutes to finish.
tips: Build weekly distance gradually. Almost every running injury comes from adding volume faster than the tendons and bones adapt, not from a single hard run.
Most of your running should be easy enough to talk in. Running every session at a middling hard pace is the fastest way to plateau.
Shorten your stride and let your cadence rise if you feel yourself thudding — reaching for a longer stride puts the brakes on with every footfall.

scapular-pull-ups.description: A straight-arm hang exercise lifting the chest by depressing and retracting the shoulder blades, building pull-up strength.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with arms fully extended.
Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Depress and retract your shoulder blades to lift your chest.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Return to a fully hanging position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Think of pulling your shoulder blades down into your back pockets.
Avoid swinging or kipping to keep the movement strict.
Focus on small, precise movement quality rather than maximum height.

seated-calf-raise.description: A machine calf raise performed seated to specifically target the soleus muscle.
instructions: Sit at a calf raise machine with the pads resting on your thighs.
Lower your heels as far as possible.
Raise up onto your toes.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: The bent knee slackens the gastrocnemius, so the soleus does more of the work.
Use a full range of motion.

seated-dumbbell-lateral-raise.description: A seated isolation exercise raising dumbbells out to the sides, targeting the side deltoids without leg drive.
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep your back upright and core braced.
Raise both dumbbells out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use a light weight to keep the raise strict.
Lead with your elbows rather than your hands.
Raise to shoulder height and lower with control.

seated-smith-machine-shoulder-press.description: A seated overhead press on the Smith machine, using the fixed bar path to keep the focus on the deltoids.
instructions: Position a bench inside a Smith machine.
Sit facing forward with the bar at shoulder height.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack and press the bar straight up until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder height with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Align the bench so the bar tracks just in front of your nose.
Brace your core to keep the lower back from over-arching.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor for a stable base.

shrug.description: An isolation movement for the upper trapezius.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell at arm's length with an overhand grip.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower your shoulders back down with control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid rolling the shoulders forward or backward at the top.
Keep your arms relaxed and let the traps do the work.
Keep your neck neutral instead of jutting the chin forward.

side-lying-hip-adduction.description: A side-lying exercise raising the bottom leg against gravity, training hip adduction with body weight alone.
instructions: Lie on your side with your bottom leg straight.
Bend your top leg and place its foot flat in front of the bottom thigh.
Support your head with your bottom arm.
Lift the bottom leg upward toward the ceiling.
Lower the leg back down under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep your hips stacked vertically to avoid rolling backward.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate through the short range of motion.
Pause briefly at the top of each lift.

side-plank-leg-lift.description: A side plank with the top leg raising up, combining lateral core work with hip abduction.
instructions: Lie on your side with the forearm on the floor, elbow under the shoulder.
Stack the feet and lift the hips into a side plank.
From this stable side plank, raise the top leg straight up toward the ceiling.
Lower the leg back down with control without dropping the hips.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep the hips lifted the entire set — do not let them sag.
Lead the leg lift with the heel, not the toes.
Keep the body in one straight line from head to bottom foot.

single-arm-dumbbell-bench-press.description: A flat-bench press performed with one dumbbell at a time. The unilateral load trains the chest, shoulder and triceps while the trunk works to keep the body from rotating off the bench.
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench with the feet planted on the floor and a dumbbell held at chest level in one hand.
Rest the free hand on your stomach or hold it out to the side for balance.
Press the dumbbell up over the chest until the arm is straight.
Pause briefly at the top without letting the body roll toward the pressing arm.
Lower the dumbbell slowly to the side of the chest.
Complete the repetitions on one side, then switch arms.
tips: Squeeze the glutes and keep the shoulder blades pinned to the bench to resist rotation.
Lower to the side of the chest, with the elbow about 45 degrees from the body.
Use a weight you can hold level without twisting; add load only when both sides match.

single-arm-plank.description: A harder plank in which one hand leaves the floor so you hold the position on a single arm. With one support gone, the trunk has to resist twisting, which works the obliques and deep abdominals far more than a standard plank.
instructions: Set up in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your feet a little wider than hip-width.
Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes to keep your body in one straight line.
Shift your weight onto one arm and lift the other hand off the floor, resting it on your hip or behind your back.
Keep your hips and shoulders level and square to the floor.
Hold for the planned time, then replace the hand and rest.
Repeat on the other arm.
tips: Place your feet wider than usual to give yourself a more stable base.
Stop the hips from twisting toward the lifted arm; the body should stay as flat as in a normal plank.
Progress by shortening the lift time first, then lengthen it as the trunk gets stronger.

single-leg-box-squat.description: A single-leg squat in which you sit back onto a box and stand up again on the same leg, with the other leg held out in front of you. The box limits the depth and gives you a target to reach, so it is a controlled way to build toward the pistol squat.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy box or bench that is about knee height, with your back to it.
Shift your weight onto one leg and lift the other leg out in front of you, with your arms stretched forward for balance.
Push your hips back and bend the standing knee, lowering yourself under control toward the box.
Sit lightly on the box without dropping onto it, keeping your chest up and the free leg off the floor.
Press through the whole standing foot and straighten that leg to stand up again.
Complete the planned repetitions, then repeat on the other leg.
tips: Choose a higher box to start; lower it as your strength and control improve.
Keep the knee of the standing leg tracking over your toes and your heel on the floor.
Touch the box with your hips rather than relaxing onto it, and use the arms as a counterweight.

single-leg-glute-bridge-hold.description: The top of the single-leg glute bridge held for time: hips extended and level while one leg is lifted, so one glute carries the whole position.
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot flat, and lift the other leg so the thigh is roughly vertical.
Push through the heel of the planted foot and lift the hips until the body is straight from the knee to the shoulders.
Level the pelvis so the lifted side does not drop, and tuck the ribs down.
Hold the top position for the prescribed time, keeping the lifted knee still.
Lower the hips under control and repeat on the other side.
tips: Watch the pelvis rather than the height: a level hip at a lower position beats a high, twisted one.
Keep the planted heel close to the glute so the hamstring does not cramp.
Extend the free leg straight if the position feels easy, but only while the pelvis stays level.

single-leg-press.description: A lower-body exercise performed on a leg press machine, pressing the platform with one leg at a time.
instructions: Sit in a leg press machine with one foot placed on the platform.
Keep the other leg off the platform, resting to the side.
Release the safeties and lower the platform by bending your knee.
Stop when your knee is near a 90-degree angle.
Drive through the heel to press the platform back up.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep your foot flat and centered on the platform.
Avoid letting your knee cave inward.
Don't lock out the knee forcefully at the top.

six-inch-hold.description: A static core hold lying on the back with the head, shoulders and straight legs lifted about six inches off the floor. It trains the lower abdominals and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs straight and the arms resting along your sides.
Press the lower back into the floor and brace the abdominals.
Lift the head, shoulders and straight legs about six inches off the floor.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
Lower slowly to rest.
tips: Keep the lower back flat; if it arches, raise the legs a little higher or bend the knees.
Keep the neck relaxed and the chin slightly tucked.
Build up with short holds and rest in between.

sled-row.description: A loaded carry-and-pull performed by holding a sled's strap handles and rowing it toward you as you walk backwards, training the back through a continuous drag rather than discrete reps.
instructions: Load a sled with two straps attached and take one strap handle in each hand.
Stand facing the sled with the arms extended and the torso leaned back slightly against the load.
Pull the sled toward you by driving the elbows back, and take a short step backwards as you do.
Extend the arms again, step back once more, and repeat the pull.
Continue for distance or time, keeping a steady pull-and-step rhythm.
tips: Keep the chest up and the back flat — let the legs carry you backwards rather than rounding over the sled.
Use a load you can move continuously; the point is a steady drag, not a maximal pull.
No straps? A rope looped around the sled works the same way.

smith-machine-calf-raise.description: A standing calf raise in the Smith machine with the bar held behind the thighs at arm's length, the guided bar keeping the movement steady.
instructions: Stand in the Smith machine with your back to the bar, set just below hip height.
Reach back and grip the bar behind your thighs with both hands, arms straight.
Unrack the bar and raise up onto the balls of your feet.
Squeeze your calves hard at the top.
Lower your heels to the floor under control (below the edge if you stand on a low platform).
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid bouncing out of the bottom stretch position.
Keep your knees straight but not forcefully locked.
Use a slow tempo through the full range rather than pumping short reps.

smith-machine-hip-thrust.description: A hip thrust with the bar running in the Smith machine guides, so the load travels in a fixed vertical line across the hips while the shoulders stay supported on a bench.
instructions: Set a flat bench inside the Smith machine, parallel to the bar and positioned so the bar will sit over your hip crease.
Set the bar low enough that you can get under it while seated on the floor, then sit with your upper back against the bench.
Slide your hips under the bar so it sits over your hip crease, pad it if you need to, and unhook it with your feet flat and about hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips until your thighs and torso form a straight line, squeezing the glutes at the top.
Lower your hips under control until they are just off the floor, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Line the bench up before you load the bar. The bar can only move straight up and down, so if the bench is out of place the bar lands on your stomach or your thighs and there is no adjusting mid-set.
Set the safety stops where the bar sits at the bottom of your range. Getting out from under a loaded Smith bar on the floor is awkward, and the stops make it a non-event.
Look at a point in front of you rather than at the ceiling. Keeping the chin tucked stops the movement turning into a lower-back arch at lockout.

smith-machine-reverse-lunge.description: A reverse lunge under a Smith machine bar, stepping one foot back into the lunge and returning it to standing each repetition while the guided bar holds the load steady.
instructions: Set the bar so it sits across your upper traps when you stand, then unrack it with your feet under your hips.
Step one foot straight back and lower the rear knee toward the floor, keeping the front shin vertical and most of your weight on the front foot.
Stop when the rear knee is just short of the floor and the front thigh is roughly parallel to it.
Push through the front heel and bring the rear foot back to standing under the bar.
Complete all the repetitions on one side, then switch legs, or alternate legs on every repetition.
tips: Step back far enough. A short step puts the front knee well past the toes, which the fixed bar path will not let you correct once you are loaded.
The stepping foot does the travelling; the front foot does not move at all. If it shifts between reps, your step is too long or too short.
The rack removes the balance, not the load -- keep the trunk braced and stand up out of the bottom rather than leaning back into the bar.

smith-machine-squat.description: A squat performed on the Smith machine, using the fixed bar path for added stability while training quads and glutes.
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height and step under it.
Position the bar across your upper traps and unrack it.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, slightly forward of the bar.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Brace your core and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Set the safety stops just below your lowest squat depth.

spider-curl.description: A curl lying face-down on an incline bench with arms hanging vertical, isolating the biceps through a strict range.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with arms hanging straight down.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Keep your upper arms vertical as you curl the weights up.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Lower the dumbbells under control to full extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your chest glued to the pad for the whole set.
Squeeze at the top without letting the elbows drift backward.
Use the full range — the stretch at the bottom is half the value.

spoto-press.description: A bench press variation pausing the bar just above the chest to build control and pressing power.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulders.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with arms extended.
Lower the bar until it is one inch above your chest.
Pause there for a full second without touching the chest.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and pinned to the bench.
Hold the bar motionless during the pause instead of letting it drift.
Use a lighter load than your standard bench press.

stability-ball-hip-bridge.description: A glute bridge with the feet on a stability ball, adding an anti-rotation and balance demand to the basic bridge pattern.
instructions: Lie face-up on the floor and place both feet on top of a stability ball.
Arms rest at the sides on the floor for balance.
Squeeze the glutes and press the heels into the ball to raise the hips.
Finish with a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Lower the hips under control without the ball rolling away.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The ball will try to drift — keep the feet pressed straight down.
No hyperextension at the top; stop when the body is in a line.

stability-ball-wall-squat.description: A bodyweight squat with a stability ball pinned between the lower back and a wall, keeping the spine guided.
instructions: Place a stability ball between your lower back and a wall.
Step the feet forward about a foot, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Squat down, letting the ball roll up the back as you descend.
Stop when thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Keep the weight in the heels and mid-foot.
Do not let the knees travel past the toes.
The ball should roll smoothly — do not lean off it.

standing-calf-stretch.description: A staggered-stance stretch that lengthens the calf by pressing the rear heel down with the back leg straight.
instructions: Step one foot back into a staggered stance.
Keep the back leg straight and the heel pressed down.
Bend the front knee and lean your weight forward.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the rear heel flat and toes pointing forward.
Bend the rear knee slightly to target the lower calf.

standing-quad-stretch.description: A standing balance stretch that lengthens the quadriceps by pulling the heel toward the glute.
instructions: Stand on one leg, holding a wall for balance if needed.
Bend the other knee and grab that ankle behind you.
Pull the heel toward your glute, keeping knees together.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Tuck your pelvis under to deepen the stretch.
Keep your knees close together throughout.

stationary-bike.description: A seated cardio machine movement that drives a flywheel through a continuous pedalling cycle, training the legs with no impact through the joints.
instructions: Set the saddle height so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke, then sit down and place the balls of your feet on the pedals.
Take the handlebars with a relaxed grip and sit tall, with your back neutral and your shoulders down.
Push one pedal down and forward while the other rises, keeping the effort in your legs rather than pulling on the bars.
Keep pedalling in a smooth, even circle at a steady cadence, breathing in rhythm with the stroke.
Adjust the resistance to hold your target effort, and continue for the desired time or distance.
tips: Set the saddle before you start: too low grinds the knees, too high rocks your hips side to side at the bottom of every stroke.
Drive with the legs and keep the upper body quiet — gripping and hauling on the bars adds nothing but neck and shoulder tension.
Raise the resistance rather than spinning the pedals loose and fast; a light flywheel at high cadence feels hard on the lungs but does little for the legs.

straight-arm-pulldown.description: An isolation exercise for the lats using a cable with arms kept straight.
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attached to the high pulley.
With arms nearly straight, push the bar down in an arc toward your thighs.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Maintain a slight elbow bend without turning the movement into a pressdown.
Hinge slightly at the hips and keep your back flat.
Avoid using body momentum to swing the bar down.

suitcase-carry.description: A loaded walk with the weight in one hand only, so the trunk has to resist bending toward the load for the whole distance — the unilateral counterpart to the farmer's walk.
instructions: Stand beside a single kettlebell or dumbbell with your feet under your hips.
Hinge at the hips, take the handle in one hand and stand up with the weight hanging at your side.
Pull that shoulder down and back, and brace as if you were about to be pushed sideways.
Walk forward with normal, even strides, keeping your torso upright and square rather than leaning away from the weight.
Keep the free arm relaxed at your side instead of sticking it out as a counterweight.
Carry for the desired distance or time, set the weight down under control, then repeat on the other side.
tips: Do the same distance on both sides. The whole value is in the asymmetry, and it only works if you load both directions equally.
If you find yourself tipping toward the weight or hiking the opposite hip, the weight is too heavy — this is a posture drill first.
Grip usually gives out before the trunk does. That is a legitimate training effect, but if it is always the limit, use straps for the heavier sets.

supine-spinal-twist.description: A lying twist that stretches the lower back, glutes and obliques by dropping a bent knee across the body.
instructions: Lie on your back and bend one knee toward your chest.
Guide that knee across your body toward the floor.
Stretch your arms out wide and turn your head away.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep both shoulders on the floor.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

svend-press.description: A plate-squeeze press that loads the pecs through isometric adduction as you extend the weight away from the chest.
instructions: Stand upright holding a single weight plate (or two pressed together) between your palms at chest height.
Squeeze the plates hard to generate tension through the pecs.
Press the plates straight out in front of you until the arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly, keeping the squeeze, then return the plates to the chest.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The harder you squeeze the plates, the more chest activation you get.
Keep the plates at sternum height throughout — do not let them drop toward the hips.

thread-the-needle.description: A kneeling rotation: one arm slides under the body and the shoulder and side of the head rest on the floor, rotating the thoracic spine passively.
instructions: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Slide one arm underneath the body, palm facing up, until the shoulder and the side of the head rest on the mat.
Keep the hips stacked over the knees and walk the top hand forward or wrap it behind the back.
Hold the twist for the prescribed time, breathing into the upper back.
Press the top hand into the floor to come up and repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep the hips high over the knees; dropping them turns the rotation into a side bend.
Rest the head on a block if the shoulder cannot reach the floor comfortably.
Let the shoulder settle with the breath instead of pushing the twist deeper by force.

toes-to-bar.description: An advanced hanging core exercise on a pull-up bar requiring hip flexion strength and lat engagement to touch the toes to the bar.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended and body still.
Engage your lats and core to prevent swinging.
Raise your legs with straight knees, reaching your toes up toward the bar.
Touch the bar with your toes, then lower your legs under control.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Initiate the movement from your core, not by kicking with momentum.
Exhale forcefully as you raise your legs to increase intra-abdominal pressure.
If you cannot reach the bar yet, build up with hanging leg raises first; they are the easier step towards it.

triangle-pose.description: A wide-stance pose with both legs straight and the torso tilting sideways over the front leg, lengthening the hamstring and the whole side body.
instructions: Stand wide with the front foot turned out and the back foot angled slightly in.
Keep both legs straight and reach the front hand forward as the hips shift back.
Tilt sideways and bring the bottom hand to the shin, a block or the floor, top arm reaching up.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, turning the chest towards the ceiling.
Press into the feet to come up and repeat on the other side.
tips: Reach out over the front leg before you tilt down; folding early collapses the pose.
Use a block under the bottom hand rather than dragging the chest towards the floor.
Keep both legs straight and the kneecaps lifted.

triceps-dip-hold-bench.description: An isometric hold at the bottom of the bench dip: with your hands on the edge of a bench behind you and your legs out in front, you lower your body and stop with the elbows bent. The triceps work hard at the point where the dip is hardest, with less load on the shoulders than a deep dip on bars.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench, place your hands next to your hips with your fingers pointing forward and walk your feet out so that your legs are straight.
Slide your hips off the bench and straighten your arms to hold your weight.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until they reach about 90 degrees, keeping your back close to the bench.
Stop there and hold, with your elbows pointing straight back and your chest open.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears while you hold for the planned time.
Press up to straight arms and sit back down.
tips: Do not drop lower than 90 degrees at the elbow; going deeper puts a lot of stress on the front of the shoulders.
Keep your back close to the bench and your elbows pointing back, not out to the sides.
Bend your knees and bring your feet closer to make the hold easier.

trx-hamstring-curl.description: This isolation exercise uses a suspension trainer to target the hamstrings, glutes, and calves by curling the heels towards the glutes.
instructions: Lie on your back with heels in the suspension trainer cradles, knees bent at 90 degrees.
Lift your hips off the floor, creating a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Extend your legs forward, maintaining hip elevation and core tension.
Pull your heels back towards your glutes, contracting your hamstrings forcefully.
Control the movement, avoiding any drop in hip height throughout the set.
tips: Keep your core braced to prevent your hips from sagging.
Focus on a strong hamstring contraction at the peak of the curl.
Control the eccentric phase by slowly extending your legs.

trx-row.description: This bodyweight pulling exercise uses a suspension trainer to target your entire back, building strength in the lats, rhomboids, and biceps.
instructions: Grasp the handles of a suspension trainer with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Lean back, extending your arms fully, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Engage your core and pull your chest towards your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Maintain a rigid body throughout the movement, avoiding any sagging in the hips.
tips: Adjust your foot position: the closer your feet are to the anchor point, the harder the exercise.
Keep your elbows close to your body to emphasize the lats, or flare them slightly for more upper back.
Focus on initiating the pull with your back muscles, not just your arms.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to maximize muscle engagement.

trx-y-fly.description: This suspension trainer exercise targets the posterior deltoids and trapezius, improving shoulder health and posture by strengthening the upper back.
instructions: Stand facing the anchor point, holding the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Lean back, extending your arms straight in front of you, maintaining a plank position with your body.
Raise your arms up and out into a 'Y' overhead, pulling your shoulder blades together and down as your body rises toward the anchor.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows throughout and squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Slowly control the descent back to the starting position, resisting the pull of the straps.
tips: Adjust your body angle to modify difficulty: leaning further back increases the challenge.
Focus on retracting and depressing your shoulder blades throughout the movement.
Maintain a rigid core and straight body line to prevent sagging hips.

v-bar-tricep-pushdown.description: A cable tricep pushdown using a V-handle, which locks the wrists in a pronated, slightly-angled position and loads the lateral head.
instructions: Attach a V-bar handle to a high cable pulley.
Stand facing the stack and grip the V-bar with both hands, palms down.
Start with the elbows tucked to the sides, forearms parallel to the floor.
Press the handle down until the arms are fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps, then return under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows pinned to the sides the entire set.
Don't lean into the bar; a small forward lean is fine, but let the triceps do the work.

walking-lunge.description: A traveling lunge stepping forward leg over leg, training the quads and glutes with an added balance challenge.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on hips.
Step one foot forward into a long lunge.
Lower until both knees are around 90 degrees.
Drive through the front heel and step the back foot forward.
Continue alternating legs as you walk forward.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lower until both knees reach about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright as you step.
Drive through your front heel to step forward smoothly.

wall-sit.description: A static isometric exercise holding a squat position against a wall to build quad endurance.
instructions: Stand with back against a wall.
Slide down until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Hold the position.
Stand back up when done.
tips: Keep knees at 90 degrees.
Press your back flat against the wall.

weighted-dips.description: A parallel-bar dip performed with extra load — most often a plate hung from a dip belt between the legs — to keep the movement in a strength rep range once bodyweight dips are easy.
instructions: Attach a plate to a dip belt around your waist so the weight hangs between your legs.
Grip the parallel dip bars and press yourself up to the top position with your arms locked out and your feet off the floor.
Lean your torso slightly forward and lower your body by bending your elbows until your shoulders are below them.
Press back up through your palms until your arms are locked out again, keeping the hanging plate from swinging.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Add weight only once you can do clean bodyweight dips through a full range — small jumps of 2.5–5 kg are enough, since the load stacks on top of your own bodyweight.
Keep your legs together and your core braced so the plate does not start swinging; a swinging weight throws off the bottom of the rep.
Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears and stop the descent if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.

wide-grip-pull-ups.description: A pull-up performed with a wide overhand grip, emphasizing the lats and upper-back width.
instructions: Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
Hang with arms fully extended and core braced.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Keep your shoulders pulled back as you rise.
Lower yourself under control to full extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Initiate each rep by depressing your shoulder blades before bending the arms.
Avoid kipping or swinging your legs for momentum.
Squeeze the bar firmly and keep your wrists straight.

wide-stance-leg-press.description: A leg press with a wide, slightly turned-out stance that increases the contribution of the adductors alongside hip and knee extension while the back stays supported.
instructions: Set the back pad and seat so your lower back remains supported at the bottom of the repetition.
Place your feet wide on the platform with the toes turned out only as far as the knees can follow comfortably.
Lower the sled by bending the hips and knees while keeping the knees aligned with the toes and the feet flat.
Press through the whole foot and extend the hips and knees without forcing the knees into lockout.
Lower the sled under control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a width and toe angle that your hips can control; wider is not automatically better.
Keep the knees moving in the same direction as the toes rather than letting them collapse inward.
Stop the descent before the pelvis rolls under and the lower back loses contact with the pad.

zercher-squat.description: A squat in which the barbell is held in the crooks of the elbows at the front of the body. The front-loaded bar keeps the torso upright and works the quadriceps, glutes, upper back and core.
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about waist height, step in and hook it into the crooks of the elbows, with the forearms crossed or the hands clasped in front of the chest.
Lift the bar out of the rack, step back and stand with the feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace the core and keep the chest up and the elbows pressed together.
Squat down by bending the hips and knees until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of the feet to stand back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then re-rack the bar.
tips: Wrap the bar in a pad or towel; the elbow crease is sensitive and can bruise.
Keep the elbows high and together so the bar does not roll toward the hands.
Keep the torso upright; if the chest drops, lower the load.
